summary: St Jean Airport (CYJN/YJN) is a general aviation airport serving Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, Quebec, about 40 km southeast of Montreal. It has roots as a military training airfield and today supports flight training, private flying, and skydiving. Its two asphalt runways and riverside location make it a convenient reliever field for the Montreal area.
faqs:
Q: Does St Jean Airport have scheduled commercial flights?
A: No. YJN is a general aviation airport with no scheduled airline service; it mainly handles private aircraft, flight training, and recreational flying.

Q: How far is St Jean Airport from Montreal?
A: It is roughly 40 km (25 mi) southeast of Montreal, typically a 35–50 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: What facilities are available at CYJN?
A: Expect basic general aviation services such as fuel, parking, and flight-school facilities; terminal amenities are limited, so plan ahead for food and ground transport.

Q: Can I fly internationally into St Jean Airport?
A: It is not a major port of entry; if you need customs, confirm availability with the airport and CBSA well before arrival.
transport_tips: By car, take Autoroute 35 to Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu and follow local signs to the airport; driving from Montreal usually takes 35–50 minutes. Taxis and rideshares can be arranged from downtown Saint-Jean-sur-Richelieu, but there is no direct rail or frequent bus service to the terminal. On-site parking is available, and rental cars should be reserved in advance.
local_tip: Skydiving and flight-training traffic can be busy on weekends, so monitor the common traffic frequency early and expect rapid runway changes; also check for morning river-valley fog before planning a VFR departure.
